Nuclear NDT training in Aiken: the short answer

Nuclear NDT training in Aiken means getting technicians certified in UT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET in a way the Savannah River Site contractors and the region's commercial nuclear owners will accept. Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A method training live online or onsite at your Aiken or Augusta-area facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. It is the certification foundation; SRS site qualification, CP-189 programmes and EPRI PDI demonstration are separate layers your employer adds.

The Central Savannah River Area is one of the few places in the country where a technician can work DOE-complex construction, high-level waste operations and a brand-new commercial nuclear plant within a short commute. That breadth is an advantage, but it also means three different quality cultures, three sets of auditors and three views of what a certification file should look like. The section below sets out who those customers are and what each expects.

Nuclear NDT work in Aiken and the CSRA

These organisations are named to describe local demand; none is an Atlantis client or partner.

  • Savannah River Site (DOE and NNSA). SRS spans DOE Environmental Management missions, including the Defense Waste Processing Facility that vitrifies high-level waste and the Salt Waste Processing Facility, and NNSA missions including tritium operations and the planned Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility for pit production, which is being built by repurposing an earlier, unfinished facility. Construction and modification of process systems generate a steady flow of weld examination, much of it on stainless steel.
  • Savannah River National Laboratory. Research and engineering work that needs fabricated test equipment and specialty components, and the examinations that go with them.
  • Plant Vogtle, Waynesboro, Georgia. Across the river, Vogtle Units 3 and 4 were the first new reactors completed in the United States in decades. With four units operating, the site brings recurring refuelling outages and the in-service examination that comes with them under ASME Section XI.
  • South Carolina's commercial fleet. The state hosts several operating nuclear plants, so outage contractors draw technicians from across the region during spring and autumn outage seasons.
  • Fabricators and suppliers. Shops in Aiken, North Augusta, Augusta and along the I-20 corridor supply the site contractors and nuclear owners, and are the most direct fit for employer-based SNT-TC-1A certification.

For non-nuclear employers in the area see NDT training in Aiken. For state-level detail see NDT training in South Carolina and, for the Augusta and Vogtle side of the river, NDT training in Georgia. The national overview is at nuclear NDT training.

NDT methods used in Aiken nuclear work

MethodNuclear application in Aiken and the CSRACode / standard context
UTWeld examination on new process piping and tanks at SRS; thickness monitoring on waste-handling systems; in-service examination at VogtleASME Section V, B31.3, Section III where invoked, Section XI at operating plants
PAUT and TOFDVolumetric weld examination where radiography conflicts with schedules, shielding or controlled areasASME Section V Article 4, owner-accepted Code Cases
RT and digital radiographyConstruction weld radiography on stainless process piping and vesselsASME Section V Article 2, construction code acceptance criteria
MTCarbon-steel structural welds, supports and lifting equipmentASME Section V Article 7, AWS D1.1
PTStainless welds in process and waste systems, using consumables with controlled halogen and sulphur contentASME Section V Article 6, site consumable controls
VTFit-up and final weld visual, remote visual in tanks and cells, Section XI VT examinations at operating plantsASME Section V Article 9, Section XI
ETSteam-generator and heat-exchanger tubing during outages; surface examination on non-ferromagnetic partsASME Section V Article 8, owner programmes

Method spotlight for Aiken: UT thickness and weld examination on waste-system tanks and piping. Long-lived waste processing systems need repeatable thickness data and weld examination that can be compared year on year. Technicians who understand calibration, coverage and documentation discipline, not just how to find a reflector, are the ones site contractors keep.

DOE-site work versus outage work: two different careers from Aiken

Technicians based in Aiken often move between two very different kinds of nuclear work, and it helps to know which one you are training for.

DOE-site work at SRS is long-horizon. Construction and modification projects, waste-processing operations and facility maintenance run year round, so the work is steadier and the employer relationship tends to last longer. The examinations are mostly fabrication-stage and construction-stage: new welds on process piping, tanks and support structures, judged against the construction code and the project specification. The quality culture is DOE's, expressed through the contractor's QA programme, and the overhead is site access, radiological work training and procedure compliance.

Outage work at operating plants is seasonal and intense. Crews mobilise for refuelling outages, work long shifts against a critical path, and demobilise. Examinations are in-service, under ASME Section XI, and the personnel requirements are stricter: CP-189-based programmes, and PDI qualification for specified UT scope. The overhead is plant access authorisation, fitness for duty and plant-specific training.

Both start from the same place: solid method certification with clean records. Technicians who build that foundation can move between the two as demand shifts, which in the CSRA it regularly does.

Which certification scheme Aiken nuclear employers expect

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Here is how that sits against the other schemes CSRA employers ask for.

SchemeWho typically requires itDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1AFabricators, construction contractors and many SRS suppliers; ASME Section III and B31 construction work commonly references itYes. Atlantis training is built around it.
DOE / NNSA site quality programme (10 CFR 830, DOE O 414.1, NQA-1)SRS management and operations and liquid-waste contractors and their suppliersUsually yes as the method-certification base, with site qualification and training added by the contractor.
ANSI/ASNT CP-189In-service examination at Vogtle and other operating plants under ASME Section XIPartly. Method knowledge carries over; the employer's programme must be written to CP-189.
EPRI PDI performance demonstrationSpecified in-service UT under Section XI Appendix VIIINo. A separate blind demonstration, taken after method certification.

ISO 9712 / ACCPRare locallyNo. Not offered by Atlantis.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path for Aiken technicians

  1. Written practice. The employer's document that defines training, experience, examinations and certification. SRS suppliers need it to sit cleanly inside the contractor's QA flow-down. See written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Documented classroom or live-online hours per method and level. See the training requirements matrix for minimums.
  3. Experience. Documented on-the-job time in each method, ideally logging materials and product forms.
  4. Examinations. General, specific and practical examinations under Level III authority, the practical on real flawed specimens.
  5. Vision examination to the written practice requirement.
  6. Certification by the employer, with recertification at the written practice interval.

Further reading: SNT-TC-1A training and certification, the Level II path and ASNT Level III training.

Radiation licensing and site access around Aiken

South Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Since July 2024, radioactive-material licensing, including industrial radiography, sits with the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SCDES), which took over these functions when the former DHEC was reorganised. Georgia is also an Agreement State, so a crew working on both sides of the Savannah River may need to think about two state licences or reciprocity.

Radiographers need radiographer certification under the state equivalent of 10 CFR Part 34 in addition to employer NDT method certification. These are often confused; you need both to expose a source.

At SRS, NRC guidance indicates that Agreement State licensees generally stay under their state's authority when working at DOE facilities, except in rare areas of exclusive federal jurisdiction. DOE's occupational radiation rule (10 CFR 835) and the site's radiological control programme govern the work environment at the same time. Confirm the arrangements for your work area with the site contractor before you mobilise a source.

Access is the other gate. SRS badging, site-specific training and, for some NNSA areas, a security clearance are site requirements independent of your NDT certification. Vogtle has its own access authorisation and fitness-for-duty process for outage workers. Employers plan these alongside training, not after it.

Online, live-virtual or onsite training for Aiken crews

Atlantis has no training centre in Aiken or anywhere else. Delivery options:

  • Live online classroom sessions, which suit technicians on site rotations or outage schedules. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility in Aiken, North Augusta or Augusta, using your equipment, procedures and specimens.
  • Blended: online theory, then onsite practicals and examinations timed around outage seasons and project milestones.

Spring and autumn outage seasons pull technicians away for weeks at a time, so many CSRA employers schedule classroom work between outages and practical examinations just before. For company cohorts see corporate NDT training. Request an Aiken nuclear training quote; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Level III services and written practices for Aiken nuclear suppliers

Flow-down audits from site contractors and nuclear owners routinely sample NDT personnel files. Typical findings: written practices that do not reflect current methods or techniques, examinations that cannot be reconstructed, missing experience logs, lapsed vision tests, and an outside Level III with no evidence of review.

Atlantis supports written-practice development, Level III examination administration, procedure review and audit readiness. See NDT consulting in Augusta, NQA-1 nuclear supplier NDT programmes, written practices for nuclear power, Level III audit support for nuclear and nuclear NDT consulting. Book a Level III consultation for your Aiken programme.

What an Aiken employer receives from a training engagement

  • Course outlines for each method and level, mapped to your written practice.
  • Signed attendance and hours records for each trainee.
  • Graded general and specific examinations, retained for audit.
  • Practical examination records identifying specimens, techniques and results.
  • A gap list for anything in your written practice, experience logs or vision records that needs fixing before you certify.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator covers 12 methods across five environments: NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. The storage-tank and welding-workshop scenes are good rehearsal for the thickness and weld work common around Aiken. It is practice only and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, with examinations administered under ASNT Level III authority in line with your written practice.

Local options compared

  • Aiken Technical College. Strong nuclear workforce programmes, including radiation protection technology and a Nuclear Fundamentals programme developed with SRS. These prepare people for radiological control and plant roles; they are not NDT method certification programmes, but they pair well with one.
  • Contractor in-house programmes. Site contractors and outage service companies certify NDT staff under their own written practices.
  • National providers. Scheduled public courses in other states, useful if you can travel and the course matches your written practice.
  • Atlantis NDT. SNT-TC-1A method training and Level III support online or onsite at your facility. Best fit for CSRA employers certifying crews without sending them out of town.

Frequently asked questions about nuclear NDT training in Aiken

How do I get nuclear NDT training in Aiken, SC?

Start with method certification, typically UT plus PT or MT to Level II, under an employer's written practice. Then pick up SRS site qualification or outage requirements through an employer that does that work. Atlantis provides the method training online or onsite.

Does the Savannah River Site accept SNT-TC-1A certification?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used as the method basis across the DOE complex, but SRS contractors set their own requirements through their quality programmes. Ask the contractor's QA organisation.

Can I take NDT training online in South Carolina?

Yes for the classroom portion. Practical training and practical examinations need real equipment and specimens at your employer's facility. See online NDT training.

Do I need a licence for radiography in South Carolina?

The company needs a radioactive-material licence from SCDES for gamma sources, and individual radiographers need radiographer certification on top of NDT method certification. Work in Georgia brings Georgia's licensing or reciprocity into play.

Can I work Vogtle outages with SNT-TC-1A certification?

Outage in-service work usually requires a CP-189-based programme, and some UT scope requires PDI qualification. The outage employer decides. SNT-TC-1A training is the foundation.

Is Aiken Technical College's radiation protection programme the same as NDT training?

No. Radiation protection technicians survey and control radiological hazards; NDT technicians examine materials and welds. The two careers work side by side, and RT technicians benefit from radiation-protection knowledge.

How long does UT Level II training take?

Minimum hours and experience are defined in SNT-TC-1A and your written practice. See the training requirements matrix. Experience is usually the longer part.

What does nuclear NDT training cost in Aiken?

Quote on request. Cost depends on methods, levels, group size, onsite or online delivery, and whether examinations or written-practice work are included. Ask for an Aiken cohort quote.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA?

Both fund approved training providers only. Atlantis does not claim that approval; check with the VA or your SC Works centre. Employer-paid training is the usual route.

Do I need a clearance to do NDT at SRS?

Some NNSA areas require a clearance; many roles need site badging and training. Your employer sponsors that process. Training does not grant access.

We are based in Augusta, Georgia. Is this page relevant to us?

Yes. Many CSRA employers sit on the Georgia side of the river and serve both SRS and Plant Vogtle. Training is delivered at your facility or online either way; the main difference is that Georgia's radioactive-material licensing applies to RT work in Georgia. See NDT training in Georgia and NDT consulting in Augusta.

What do NDT technicians earn in the CSRA?

It varies by employer, method, level and outage work. See the NDT salary guide for published ranges.

Preparing for written exams? Work through UT Level 2 practice questions and rehearse scanning on the Practical NDT simulator.
